sentences.text: The learned senior counsel for the petitioner submits that even if the allegations of the complainant are taken at the highest, no offence under Section 376 of the IPC is made out.

7. He submits that the complainant herself has stated that she started residing with the petitioner on her own free will when the parties, despite being married with their respective partners, decided to have a romantic consensual relationship with each other.
8. He submits that the complaint itself records that after certain time elapsed, the parties had differences.

He submits that friction between parties staying together is normal in any relationship,
however, the same cannot be a ground for framing charge for an offence as serious as Section 376 of the IPC.
9. Issue notice.
10. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State accepts notice.
11. Notice be served to Respondent No. 2 / complainant though the Investigating Officer.

12. List on 29.01.2026.
AMIT MAHAJAN, J DECEMBER 22, 2025 'KDK'

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The learned senior counsel for the petitioner submits that even if the allegations of the complainant are taken at the highest, no offence under Section 376 of the IPC is made out.
7. He submits that the complainant herself has stated that she started residing with the petitioner on her own free will when the parties, despite being married with their respective partners, decided to have a romantic consensual relationship with each other.
8. He submits that the complaint itself records that after certain time elapsed, the parties had differences.
He submits that friction between parties staying together is normal in any relationship,
however, the same cannot be a ground for framing charge for an offence as serious as Section 376 of the IPC.
